{{Quote|Some of you have reported hearing increased gabble on the Neo helmet's Z-band. Just ignore it.|Koblus Sornell|<ref name="Interference" />}}
The '''Z-band''' was a range of [[Subspace transceiver/Legends|subspace transceiver]] frequencies picked up by the [[Neo-Crusader armor|helmets]] of [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders]]. During the [[Mandalorian Wars]], Neo-Crusaders relied upon the Z-band for information concerning [[Bomb/Legends|bombing]] traffic.<ref name="Interference">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/fiction/interference20090929.html|text="Interference"|int=Interference|newhost=Suvudu}}</ref>

Early in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[3963 BBY]], "[[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Benegryph Goodvalor]]" broadcasted a series of [[Propaganda/Legends|propaganda]] messages to [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] warriors using the Z-band.<ref name="Interference" /> Goodvalor was, in fact, a fictional [[Republic Navy/Legends|naval]] [[Republic officer/Legends|officer]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the Mandalorians' opposing faction in the Mandalorian Wars, based on the "heroics" of the [[Snivvian/Legends|Snivvian]] crook and entrepreneur [[Marn Hierogryph]] at the [[Battle of Serroco]]. Hierogryph and [[Gender/Legends|his]] [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] cohort, [[Slyssk]], commandeered a Republic [[Troop transport/Legends|troop transport]] landed on [[Serroco]] as Mandalorian [[Missile/Legends|missiles]] raced toward the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] surface, incidentally saving half a [[Battalion/Legends|battalion]] in the process. Thus, the character of Goodvalor was born,<ref name="KOTOR 47">[[Knights of the Old Republic 47|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 47]]</ref> as was "[[Slyssk|Commander True]]," the captain's [[Executive officer/Legends|first officer]]<ref name="Interference" /> who was based upon Slyssk.<ref name="KOTOR 47" />

Goodvalor's Z-band broadcasts,<ref name="Interference" /> where he was voiced by [[Marn Hierogryph's brother]],<ref name="KOTOR 47" /> sought to dishearten the Mandalorians and cause some of them to reconsider their allegiance in the conflict. On one occasion Commander True, rather than Captain Goodvalor, made a broadcast to the Z-band, claiming that the captain was too preoccupied with the numerous Mandalorian turncoats that had joined the Republic following his previous message to broadcast himself that [[Standard day/Legends|day]].<ref name="Interference" />

During this [[time]], Mandalorian warrior and signals expert [[Koblus Sornell]] made use of the Z-band to keep her fellow Neo-Crusaders informed of the war effort, urging them to disregard Goodvalor's "gabble" but to still listen to the Z-band to stay informed of bombing traffic. During their invasion of [[Zongorlu]], the Mandalorians came across a small room containing a directional transmitter, where "Goodvalor" had been sending his broadcasts from, though he himself had departed before the Mandalorians had arrived. Goodvalor soon resumed his messaging, proposing a one-time ceasefire deal with the Mandalorians.<ref name="Interference" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Z-band's first and only appearance is in the short story "[[Interference]]," authored by [[John Jackson Miller]]<ref name="Interference" /> and originally released to members of the [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace ''Star Wars'' fan club]]<ref name="JJM notes">{{Faraway|url=fiction/shortstories/sw-interference.html|text=''Star Wars: "Interference"''}}</ref> in [[2008]]. "Interference" serves as a tie-in to the [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic (comic series)|''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series,<ref name="Interference" /> also written by Miller,<ref name="KOTOR 1">[[Knights of the Old Republic 1|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 1]]</ref> set between the series' [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic Volume 4: Daze of Hate, Knights of Suffering|fourth]] and [[Star Wars: Vector Volume 1|fifth]] volumes.<ref name="Interference" />
